test_title: PYST 5: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 29 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: Which act introduced separate electorates for Hindus and Muslims in British India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Morley-Minto Reforms 1909**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Morley-Minto Reforms**, officially known as the **Indian Councils Act 1909**, introduced the system of **separate electorates** for **Muslims** in **British India**. This meant that **Muslim** representatives were to be elected exclusively by **Muslim voters**.

• The act was named after **Lord Morley**, the then **Secretary of State for India**, and **Lord Minto**, the then **Viceroy of India**. Due to the introduction of this communal representation, **Lord Minto** is often referred to as the **'Father of Communal Electorate'**.

• The **Indian Councils Act 1892** is incorrect because it primarily focused on increasing the number of members in the **Legislative Councils** and introduced a limited and indirect use of **elections**, but it did not establish **separate electorates** based on religion.

• The **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms 1919** (or the **Government of India Act 1919**) is incorrect as the starting point because it **extended** the principle of **separate electorates** to other communities like **Sikhs**, **Indian Christians**, **Anglo-Indians**, and **Europeans**, rather than introducing it.

• The **Government of India Act 1935** is incorrect because it was a much later piece of legislation that introduced **Provincial Autonomy** and further extended **separate electorates** to **depressed classes (scheduled castes)**, **women**, and **labor**.

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Simla Deputation (1906)**: A group of **Muslim** leaders led by the **Aga Khan** met **Lord Minto** in **October 1906** to demand **separate electorates** and **proportional representation** for **Muslims**, which heavily influenced the **1909 reforms**.

• **Expansion of Councils**: The **1909 Act** significantly increased the size of the **Legislative Councils**. The number of members in the **Central Legislative Council** was raised from **16 to 60**.

• **Indian Participation**: For the first time, the act provided for the association of **Indians** with the **Executive Councils** of the **Viceroy** and **Governors**. **Satyendra Prasad Sinha** became the first **Indian** to join the **Viceroy’s Executive Council** as a **Law Member**.

• **Powers of Legislators**: The act empowered members of the **Legislative Councils** to ask **supplementary questions** and move **resolutions** on the **budget**, although they were not allowed to vote on the budget as a whole.

**Important Points__**

• The **1919 Act** introduced **Dyarchy** in the provinces, which divided provincial subjects into two parts: **'Transferred'** and **'Reserved'**. This was a major step toward **responsible government** in **India**.

• The **1935 Act** proposed the establishment of an **All-India Federation** consisting of **Provinces** and **Princely States**. It also abolished **Dyarchy** in the provinces and introduced **Provincial Autonomy**.

• The **Indian Councils Act 1892** allowed the councils to discuss the **annual financial statement** (budget) and address questions to the **Executive**, which was a significant advancement over the **1861 Act**.

• The introduction of **separate electorates** in **1909** is widely viewed by historians as a part of the British **'Divide and Rule'** policy, which eventually contributed to the **partition of India** in **1947**.
